correctness.rationale: For the specified Lactin-2 curve, H_L(t)=(t-L)r'(t)-r(t)+r(L) increases from zero to a positive value at the inflection and then strictly decreases, with H_L(T_p)=r(L)-r(T_p)<0. Its zero gives the unique contact and the strict maximum of the secant slope. The truncated optimal chord is therefore from L to min(U,τ_L); when U>τ_L the rest of the least concave majorant is the strictly concave rate curve. Equality in pointwise majorization and Jensen's inequality forces exactly the asserted laws, including the pure law at m=τ_L and at interval endpoints. Implicit differentiation gives τ'_L<0. With t=θ+kh and h=θ-L, H_L(t)/h³ extends smoothly to h=0 with value r'''(θ)(k+1)²(2k-1)/6. Its simple root at k=1/2 and the unique contact justify the expansion by the implicit function theorem. The matching slope on the cold branch similarly gives (v_L-θ)/h=-1/2+O(h); the uniform local cubic gain is -r'''(θ)h³(s+1)(s-1/2)²/6+O(h⁴), giving -r'''(θ)/12 at the maximum. This last limit is for fixed U>θ. An independent numerical maximization of the secant and gain at h=5,1,0.2 corroborated the formula; it is not the proof. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and CHECK.py without executing the supplied script. The theorem is about distributions, not uniqueness of the ordering of a schedule.

value.rationale: For a standard developmental rate model, the result answers whether enlarging a hard upper temperature bound can improve the best rate at a fixed mean; it identifies exactly when it stops helping and quantifies the gain as the cold bound approaches the inflection. A sign-of-curvature Jensen observation alone cannot supply that sharp transition or the magnitude. The optimum is an idealized rate-summation benchmark, not evidence for field interventions or fitness, acclimation, survival, switching cost, or real-world chronology.
